claim.why_it_matters: Same page-boundary defect, and especially misleading here because Linear_A and Linear_B are near-identical names: the Linear_B ranges at the top of page 986 appear with no label at all while 'Linear_B:' sits at the end of the Linear_A line.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages at 300 dpi. PDF page 1015 (printed 985) ends its body with exactly two lines -- 'Linear_A:' and '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767' -- followed by roughly two inches of white space and then the footer '(c)ISO/IEC 2023   985'. The token 'Linear_B:' is demonstrably NOT printed anywhere on page 985. PDF page 1016 (printed 986) opens its body with 'Linear_B:' on its own line, then '10000-1000B, 1000D-10026, 10028-1003A, 1003C-1003D, 1003F-1004D, 10050-1005D,' / '10080-100FA'. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40454) instead reads '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:' and then, after the page-1016 anchor and heading, line 40460 begins with the bare ranges '10000-1000B, ...' with no script label. So the transcription pulled a real content token (a UCS script name, one of the entries this list is keyed by) backwards across the page boundary and concatenated it onto the end of a different script's range list. This is not page-break furniture, line wrapping, or hyphenation: the affected token is data, not running-head or folio material, and the relocation changes meaning in both directions -- Linear_A's range line acquires a trailing foreign label, and Linear_B's ranges are left orphaned with no key. A consumer parsing this list on the documented 'label line / ranges line' shape mis-parses both entries. Verified as a systematic pattern, not a one-off: the immediately preceding page boundary shows the identical join at line 40444, 'A984-A9B2 Kaithi:' (PDF page 985 opens with 'Kaithi:' on its own line above '11083-110AF', and the markdown for page 1015 correspondingly starts with a label-less '11083-110AF' at line 40449); line 49263 shows another, '10280-1029C Lydian:'. Note the ranges themselves are transcribed accurately -- no digits are lost -- and a separate combined script table later in the document (lines 49252-49257) does carry 'Linear_A:' and 'Linear_B:' correctly on their own lines, but that is a different table and does not repair this one. Claim quotations are accurate except for one immaterial detail: the markdown's page-1016 heading is actually '# ISO\IEC 1989:2023 (E)' with a backslash, not the forward slash the claim shows.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED as described, with one wording correction. The script label 'Linear_B:' printed at the top of PDF page 986 was transcribed at the end of page 1015 instead, appended to Linear_A's range line (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:40454 -- '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:'), leaving the Linear_B code-point ranges at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:40460 with no script label. The text is displaced, not deleted -- no code-point ranges are lost or altered -- but the label/data association is broken for two adjacent entries. This is one instance of a systematic page-boundary join defect in the UCS script tables; sibling instances confirmed at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:40444 ('A984-A9B2 Kaithi:', boundary 1014/1015) and :49263 ('10280-1029C Lydian:'). The claim's markdown quotation renders the page-1016 heading with a forward slash; the file actually contains a backslash ('# ISO\IEC 1989:2023 (E)'), which is immaterial to this finding but is itself a separate transcription artifact.
